summary: WAYLOAM v0.3.0.alpha replaces the prototype route with real OpenStreetMap-based planning, useful route services, persistent multi-day stages and a live GPS ride view.
highlights: Build real bicycle routes from place names with OpenStreetMap geocoding and BRouter profiles for Direct, Touring and Bikepacking.
Preview the generated route on a native MapLibre map with an elevation profile and nearby water, food, repair, camp and shelter points.
Split long rides around the daily target, prefer useful camps/shelters/towns near stage boundaries, and adjust day boundaries by 5 km without rebuilding the route.
Track live position, completed and remaining distance, ride ETA, off-route distance and the next useful waypoint in Ride mode.
added: Persistent route geometry, discovered route services and custom stage boundaries.
Automatic multi-day stage splitting with useful-stop preference near daily targets.
Elevation profile visualization from BRouter route geometry.
Route-corridor OpenStreetMap services for water, food, bicycle repair, camps and shelters.
Live Android GPS tracking with an on-route/off-route state and next-waypoint cue.
MapLibre route/service rendering with OpenStreetMap/OpenFreeMap attribution.
Route math tests for stage coverage, useful stops, boundary edits and projected ride progress.
changed: Fresh installs start with an empty trip instead of demo Heidelberg and Oslo locations.
Home reflects the real active trip and shows a clean empty state when no route exists.
The daily-target slider has a more visible inactive segment while keeping the WAYLOAM palette.
Settings appearance controls are flatter and less visually nested.
System and navigation bars are transparent edge-to-edge to remove the Settings bottom strip.
The top WAYLOAM mark is smaller and better balanced.
fixed: The updater now compares the manifest against the package version Android actually has installed.
Returning from the unknown-app-source permission screen resumes the APK installer automatically.
The updater opens Android's package installer directly instead of sending the user to the Downloads folder.
Android back from a secondary section returns to Home before exiting.
The active trip, current section, services and manual stage edits survive normal app recreation.
